aboutH2: Centre Espoir et Équilibre / Centre for Hope and Harmony: Detox and Live-In Treatment in Campbellton, New Brunswick
intro: Centre Espoir et Équilibre / Centre for Hope and Harmony is a Public rehab located in Campbellton, New Brunswick. Centre Espoir et Équilibre / Centre for Hope and Harmony specializes in the treatment of substance, drug and alcohol abuse.

Vitalité Health Network opened the centre on Lily Lake Road in September 2023, replacing the addiction service our directory first listed on Gallant Drive. It runs two services in French and English: a six-bed Detoxification Service and the Provincial Live-In Concurrent Disorder Treatment Service, which is growing from 12 to 18 beds and takes people from across New Brunswick. Taking part is voluntary.

pillars.title: A Purpose-Built Centre on Lily Lake Road
pillars.body: The Centre for Hope and Harmony is a $24.5 million building that opened in Campbellton in September 2023, next to the Campbellton Regional Hospital on Lily Lake Road. It has 24 single rooms, family rooms, a cafeteria, therapy rooms, a gym, a games room, a multicultural space, outdoor areas and a smudge room. Vitalité says health professionals, former patients and nearby communities, including Eel River Bar and Listuguj First Nations, helped shape the building and its programs.

pillars.title: Detox First, Then Live-In Treatment if You Need It
pillars.body: The Detoxification Service is for people 16 and over with substance use or gambling problems, and you can call to request admission yourself. Stays are mainly for medically supervised withdrawal and run about 7 to 10 days, with medical and psychosocial assessments and educational sessions. The Provincial Live-In Concurrent Disorder Treatment Service is for adults 19 and over who also have moderate mental health issues. Its core program is five weeks, with up to 30 hours a week of group and individual work, and the team can extend it.

pillars.title: Two-Eyed Seeing and a Bilingual Team
pillars.body: The centre follows Etuaptmumk, or Two-Eyed Seeing, which puts First Nations traditional knowledge, medicines and ceremonies alongside modern medicine. A sweat lodge and smudging are part of its services, and First Nations artists decorated the smudge room. The live-in program is described by Vitalité as recovery-based, trauma-informed, gender-informed and culturally informed, with a focus on reducing harm. Clinical coordinators, physicians, psychiatrists, nurses, psychologists, social workers, occupational therapists and community integration workers make up the team, and they work in both official languages.

overviewH2: Centre Espoir et Équilibre / Centre for Hope and Harmony: Centre Overview
overview: Each person in the live-in program gets an individual intervention plan built by a multidisciplinary, bilingual team. Vitalité says the plans cover support services, strategies to lower the risk of relapse and preparation for going home. The service is meant to help people reduce and manage substance use, gambling and mental health problems and improve their quality of life.

Moncton and Fredericton are each about three and a quarter hours away by car, Bathurst is about an hour, Dalhousie about 20 minutes, and Listuguj, Quebec, is just over the bridge across the Restigouche River.

faqIntro: Answers come from Vitalité Health Network's own pages about the centre and its services. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: What services does the Centre for Hope and Harmony offer?
faqs.a: The centre runs two Vitalité Health Network services: a Detoxification Service and the Provincial Live-In Concurrent Disorder Treatment Service. Both are offered in English and French, and taking part is voluntary.

faqs.q: Who can use the detox service?
faqs.a: Vitalité says the Detoxification Service is for people aged 16 and over with substance use or gambling problems. During the stay, people have medical and psychosocial assessments and attend educational sessions. The centre has six detox beds.

faqs.q: How long is a detox stay?
faqs.a: When the centre opened, Vitalité said the detox program is mainly there to provide medical supervision of withdrawal during a stay of 7 to 10 days.

faqs.q: How do I get into detox?
faqs.a: You can call yourself to ask for admission to the Detoxification Service, according to Vitalité. The centre's number is 506-789-7055, and the Restigouche Zone line is 506-789-5000.

faqs.q: Who is the live-in treatment program for?
faqs.a: The Provincial Live-In Concurrent Disorder Treatment Service is for adults aged 19 and over with serious substance use or gambling problems and moderate mental health issues, whose needs are best met in a live-in setting. It has a provincial mandate, so it takes people from across New Brunswick.

faqs.q: How long is the live-in program?
faqs.a: The core program lasts five weeks, and the team can extend it to fit each person's treatment goals. At the 2023 opening, Vitalité described stays of 35 to 90 days. Participants get up to 30 hours of group and individual services a week.

faqs.q: How do I get referred to the live-in program?
faqs.a: Vitalité recommends that a health professional who can follow you after your stay makes the request. Referrals can come from primary care, single-session therapy, the Detoxification Service, acute psychiatric units or correctional centres.

faqs.q: Are services available in French and English?
faqs.a: Yes. Vitalité says the centre offers both of its services in both official languages, and the care team is bilingual.

faqs.q: Does the centre offer Indigenous or culture-based care?
faqs.a: Yes. The centre follows Two-Eyed Seeing (Etuaptmumk), which brings together First Nations traditional knowledge, medicines and ceremonies with modern medicine. It has a sweat lodge and a smudge room decorated by First Nations artists, and Eel River Bar and Listuguj First Nations were consulted on its design.

faqs.q: Where is the centre and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The centre is at 189A Lily Lake Road in Campbellton, in New Brunswick's Restigouche region, close to the Campbellton Regional Hospital. Bathurst is about an hour away by car, and Moncton and Fredericton are each about three and a quarter hours. Listuguj, Quebec, is just across the Restigouche River.

faqs.q: Is the Centre for Hope and Harmony a public service?
faqs.a: Yes. It is run by Vitalité Health Network, one of New Brunswick's two public regional health authorities. Vitalité's pages do not list any fee for these services, so call the centre if you have questions about cost.

faqs.q: Did the centre used to be on Gallant Drive?
faqs.a: Yes. Campbellton's addiction treatment service was listed at 53 Gallant Drive before the new Centre for Hope and Harmony opened on Lily Lake Road in September 2023. The phone number, 506-789-7055, stayed the same.
